name: Pale of Calais
native: Pays reconquis (French name for the area after 1558)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of France
predecessors.text: the town of Calais, surrendered on 3 August 1347 after a siege from 4 September 1346

successors.name: Royal domain of France
successors.text: 'incorporation of Calais into the Crown lands under the leadership of Henry II' (Crown lands page)

ledger.x: 3 August 1347: Calais surrenders to Edward III and becomes English.
8 May 1360: the Treaty of Brétigny confirms English sovereignty and adds the land around Calais.
7 January 1558: the Duke of Guise takes Calais and the Pale is lost.
January 1558: English rule in France ends.

wars.name: Siege of Calais (1346-1347)
wars.outcome: Edward III took Calais on 3 August 1347 after the siege that began on 4 September 1346; the French population was expelled and the town became an English base for the rest of the Hundred Years' War and beyond.

wars.name: Siege of Calais (1558)
wars.outcome: The Duke of Guise took Calais in a week (1-7 January 1558); Guînes and Hames fell soon after, ending English rule in France.

certainty.note: The page says the Pale's boundaries 'often changed and were ill-defined' and the French kept retaking land, especially in the southwest.
